Subject: Clarify how March true-up will treat short streaming calls

Hi Marissa,

We're finishing our procurement review and want to confirm how the March true-up will be calculated for the pilot. Two quick items:

1) We have a lot of short-lived streaming interactions (typical session ~18s) that send a heartbeat every 10s. Do those heartbeats get billed as separate per-call minimums, or do you anchor them to the parent conversation for minimum/rounding?

2) How do you round token charges when sessions are very short (50-300 tokens)? Our finance team is worried about lots of tiny lines on the invoice.

I've attached a small sample of our usage for February (acme-usage-sample.csv) to give you a sense of distribution.

Can you sketch how the March true-up would look and share a sample calculation? We want to be sure the committed minimums we agreed to in the SOW don't unexpectedly overcharge for these heartbeats.

Thanks,
Susan

Hi Susan,

Thanks for the sample — that distribution is really helpful. TL;DR: we don't bill every heartbeat as a standalone minimum if it's part of an active conversation within the same connection. We apply what we call "heartbeat anchoring" (described below) to avoid micro-invoice noise. I'll attach a worked spreadsheet (acme-billing-example.xlsx) with three alternate true-up methods so you can pick the behavior that matches your accounting policy.

Quick summary:
- Heartbeat anchoring: heartbeats emitted during an active conversation window (30s inactivity threshold) are collapsed and attributed to the parent session for rounding.
- Prorate / quantum: we round token charges to a 3-token quantum for per-call accounting and to a 100-token quantum when we roll up into invoice line items for readability.
- Month-end true-up: committed minimums are compared against aggregated usage after quantum rounding; any shortfall is invoiced as a single true-up line.

I'll need one more datapoint from your side: approximate prefix reuse rate (how often calls reuse context from prior calls) — that affects KV cache credits in the sheet. If you prefer, I can run the attached spreadsheet against your sample usage and send back the filled outputs.

Attachment: acme-billing-example.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)

Ben / Kim / Susan — attaching the populated workbook and a short write-up; paste of the key worked example below so it lives in the thread.

Worked example (from the attached sheet):
Scenario: 1,200 short sessions in a day; average tokens per session = 120; heartbeats during session every 10s; inactivity timeout = 30s (heartbeat anchoring applies).

Step A — per-call accounting (internal):
- Raw tokens (sum): 144,000 tokens/day
- Per-call rounding: round each session to nearest 3-token quantum => effective billed tokens (sum after per-call quantum) = 144,006 tokens (tiny net increase due to rounding up fractional quanta).

Step B — invoice roll-up (customer-facing):
- We collapse anchored heartbeats into parent sessions (no separate per-heartbeat minimums).
- We then roll up daily usage into invoice lines with a 100-token invoice quantum to keep line-item counts low. So the 144,006 tokens rounds to 144,000 tokens on the invoice (to the nearest 100 token).

Step C — committed minimum true-up (monthly):
- Contract commit: 4,000,000 tokens/month
- Aggregated month after invoice-quantum rounding: 3,870,000 tokens
- Shortfall = 130,000 tokens -> single true-up line on the month-end invoice for 130,000 tokens (applied at the contract SKU rate).

Notes / rationale:
- The dual-quantum approach (small quantum for deterministic metering; larger quantum for invoice readability) lets us keep internal accuracy while keeping AP happy.
- Heartbeat anchoring prevents the short streaming interactions from being billed as many micro-calls; customers still pay for the actual token consumption but avoid micro line noise.
- We can optionally apply a modest "anchoring credit" (50% of the first heartbeat's quantum) as a one-off concession for pilots if you'd like a softer landing.

Attachments: acme-billing-example.xlsx, sample-invoice.pdf

If this mechanics look good, I'll draft a one-paragraph invoice note we can include on the SOW and a one-pager for Acme AP to help reconcile.

Best,
Marissa
